Every tree on n labeled nodes is equally likely, so the shapes vary freely, but each one has n - 1 edges and no cycles." width="100%"} Every one of the `n ** (n - 2)` labeled trees on `n` nodes (Cayley's formula) is equally likely. The tree is built by drawing a uniformly random Prüfer sequence, `n - 2` entries each chosen from the `n` nodes, and decoding it, so a node's degree is one more than the number of times it appears in the sequence. Random labeled trees are bushy rather than path-like or star-like: their diameter grows like the square root of `n` and their largest degree grows only slowly. The process follows NetworkX's `random_labeled_tree()`. In a directed graph every edge points from the earlier-created node to the later one. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Random labeled trees are useful for: - unbiased test inputs for tree algorithms - null models for observed trees, e.g. comparing diameters or degree distributions - random spanning structures to build other graphs from ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes. Must be at least `1`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n=` is less than `1`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A tree on `n` nodes always has `n - 1` edges: ::: {#48348d81 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_random_labeled_tree(n=50, seed=12) graph.count_edges(), graph.is_tree() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (49, True) ``` ::: ::: Its Prüfer sequence, recovered with `to_prufer_sequence()`, has `n - 2` entries: ::: {#61b5f580 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} len(graph.to_prufer_sequence()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 48 ``` ::: ::: The diameter is typically far from both extremes, `2` for a star and `49` for a path: ::: {#1922cf55 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_diameter() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 19 ``` ::: :::
